title: Customer Communication Tonebook and Staged Status Templates for LLM Degradations
author: Amelia Ortiz
content:
Summary:
This document is a practical tonebook and set of staged status-page + customer communication templates tailored for incidents that affect LLM output quality, correctness, or content-safety characteristics (e.g., hallucination spike, safety regression, semantic drift). It codifies roles, escalation triggers, timing expectations, and concrete message language we use for public status updates, customer-targeted emails, and account-level notifications.

Intro and scope:
- Audience: customer success, on-call engineers, incident bridge operators, support, and product leadership.
- Applies to: incidents where customer-visible model output quality or safety degrades beyond expected SLOs (quality SLOs, hallucination rate thresholds, content-safety flags).
- Not for: routine latency/availability incidents unless they directly cause substantive quality regressions.

Definitions and triggers (quick reference):
- Quality degradation: automated eval suite or customer telemetry indicates >15% relative regression on truthfulness/accuracy metrics vs baseline for a rolling 1-hour window.
- Safety regression: increase in content-policy flags or moderated requests >10 requests/hour above baseline for a pop >1k users.
- Hallucination spike: user-reported or eval-derived false-assertion rate >5% absolute increase for a monitored prompt-set.
- Immediate customer-impact threshold: any degradation causing production responses to be misleading or unsafe for a paying customer (requires immediate comms).

Ownership and roles:
1) Bridge Operator (primary): starts the incident bridge, coordinates responders, crafts status updates. Owner: oncall engineer on the serving runtime team.
2) Comms Lead (CS or Support): owns external messaging cadence and templates, coordinates account-level outreach. Owner: customer-success oncall.
3) Technical Lead: engineers who drive root-cause work and mitigation. Owner: eng-serving-runtime/ML infra.
4) Product/Policy Liaison: advises on messaging for safety/regulatory exposures. Owner: product or security as needed.

Incident lifecycle and communication cadence (numbered SOP):
1. Detection & Triage (0–15 minutes)
   - Bridge operator confirms signal (automated alert / customer report / eval harness).
   - Create incident in tracker and set impact level (P0/P1). If customer-facing incorrect outputs: escalate to P0.
   - If P0/P1, Comms Lead drafts a one-line internal summary and schedules a 30m bridge.

2. Rapid mitigation and visibility (15–60 minutes)
   - Technical Lead attempts immediate mitigations: model rollback, restrict generation features, enable conservative decoding, or apply safety filters.
   - Bridge operator posts first public status update (see Template A) on status.redwood.ai and internal slack #incidents.
   - Comms Lead identifies high-risk customers and triggers account-level heads-up (Template B minimal).

3. Contain & Stabilize (1–6 hours)
   - Continue mitigations and run focused evaluation runs against known prompt-sets.
   - Post hourly status updates while impact persists, moving to every-2-hours after 6 hours if stable.
   - If mitigation requires long-term config change, schedule maintenance window communications and customer Q&A.

4. Root cause & remediation (6 hours–7 days)
   - Technical Lead documents RCA draft in incident tracker, includes eval evidence, logs, and config diffs.
   - Comms Lead prepares a follow-up public note and customer-facing summary once RCA is agreed.

5. Postmortem & long-term customer outreach (7–30 days)
   - Full postmortem published with timeline, impact, and preventive actions.
   - For affected customers: offer personalized remediation notes and recommended model settings.

Tone guidance (tonebook):
- Principles: Clear, factual, accountable, low-jargon for customer notices, and technically precise for public technical notes.
- Do not speculate about root cause in initial updates. Focus on what we know and what we are doing.
- Use active voice: e.g., "We identified increased false assertions in model X and have rolled back the model variant."
- Safety incidents: prioritize customer safety language and immediate mitigation steps. Include contact path for urgent safety escalations.

Templates
- Template A: Public status page (first notice)
  Short summary: "We are investigating an elevated rate of incorrect or misleading responses from hosted text-generation (model: redwood-xyz). Some customers may see inaccurate outputs. We have started mitigation and will provide updates every 60 minutes."
  Impact: "Partial degradation: select generation traffic may return incorrect answers; latency unaffected."
  Next update: "We will update by 15:45 UTC, or sooner if there is a material change."
  Actions in progress: "Rolling back to previous verified model variant, enabling stricter safety filters, and running targeted evals."
  Contact: "For support, contact support@redwood.ai or your account lead. Critical safety issues: +1-555-0100 (pager)."

- Template B: Account-level heads-up (minimal) — Send via email/CRM
  Subject: "Heads-up: Potential incorrect responses affecting your Redwood-powered feature"
  Body (short): "Hi <CustomerName>, we are investigating reports of incorrect responses affecting text generation. Our engineers have enabled protective filters and are rolling back the most recent model variant. We will follow up with an update within 60 minutes and a full summary once we have confirmed the impact. If you see content that presents a safety risk, please reply to this message and mark as URGENT."

- Template C: Account-level detailed follow-up (post-stabilization)
  Subject: "Incident summary: Model output quality degradation on <date> — <short impact statement>"
  Body: "Hi <CustomerName>,
  What happened: We observed a spike in incorrect outputs from model <model-id> between <start> and <end>.
  Impact: <concise effect on customer workflows>.
  What we did: rolled back to <model-id-v>, applied stricter decoding constraints (top-p 0.6 / temperature 0.2), and added an automated prompt-set filter.
  Next steps: <planned preventive actions and date for follow-up>.
  If you need additional support or logs for your team, please contact <account-lead-email> and we will prioritize a technical debrief."

- Template D: Safety-regression urgent notice (for regulated customers)
  Subject: "URGENT: Safety-related regression detected and mitigations applied"
  Body: "We detected a safety-related regression that may affect user-facing content. We have disabled the affected model variant, engaged product policy, and activated manual review for flagged outputs. We recommend temporarily disabling automated production writes that depend on model-generated content until we confirm remediation. Contact: <safety-pager> or <security@redwood.ai>."

Message examples and replacements (variables to fill):
- <model-id>, <start>, <end>, <CustomerName>, <account-lead-email>, <safety-pager>.

Escalation matrix (table):
| Trigger | Bridge action | Comms cadence | Escalation owner |
|--------|---------------|---------------|------------------|
| Initial confirmed degradation | Open bridge, first status | 0, +60m | Bridge operator |
| Quality regression meeting threshold (>15%) | Immediate account-level heads-up | 0, +60m, hourly | Comms Lead |
| Safety regression | Activate Safety Liaison & security pager | Immediate, 30m | Product/Policy Liaison |
| Multi-region customer impact | Open exec brief and legal notification | 0, 30m, 2h | VP Ops/Legal |

Operational quick-checklist (to paste into bridge):
- Does the alert correspond to increased eval failures or user reports?
- Can we rollback to a verified variant? If yes, schedule rollback immediately.
- Are safety filters available? Toggle on and measure delta.
- Identify top-10 affected customers and begin targeted outreach.
- Document all comms in the incident tracker and mark public statements for legal review if required.

Examples of conservative mitigations (technical):
- Rollback to last verified model artifact.
- Enforce conservative decoding: temperature <=0.2, top-p <=0.6, max tokens limit.
- Turn on prefix/KV caching with validation layer that rejects low-confidence completions.
- Apply post-generation safety heuristics and deterministic rerankers for factuality-sensitive endpoints.

Measuring communication effectiveness (post-incident):
- CS follow-up survey: Did the notification arrive in time? (Y/N)
- TTR (time to remediate) vs. time to first public update: target <30 minutes.
- Customer satisfaction follow-up score target: >=4/5 for major incidents after remediation and debrief.

Playbook updates and ownership:
- This tonebook is maintained by Customer Success with quarterly reviews aligned to incident learnings.
- Change requests should be sent to the document owner (Amelia Ortiz) and will be reviewed by the comms reviewers list.

Appendices
A. Example timeline snippet (concrete)
- 14:02 UTC: Automated eval detects a 22% regression on truthfulness for prompt-set A. Pager triggered.
- 14:05 UTC: Bridge opened by oncall. First internal notif sent.
- 14:12 UTC: Rollback initiated to model v1.8. Safety filter enabled.
- 14:35 UTC: Public status posted (Template A).
- 15:40 UTC: Mitigation verified; affected customers emailed (Template C draft).

B. Internal slack channel guidance
- Use #incidents-bridge-<incident-id> for technical chatter and #incidents-comm for external message drafts.
- Pin final status updates and mark each message with [STATUS] and the update timestamp.

C. Quick link list (operational)
- Incident tracker: https://tracker.redwood.ai/incident/<id>
- Status page editor: https://status.redwood.ai/admin
- Pager and oncall: https://oncall.redwood.ai

End of document.
